name: Documented current-account conversion, then wire the USD out
who: US citizen with lawful RMB current-account income in a mainland bank (salary, fees, etc.)
legal_basis: Current Account FX Business Guidelines 2020, 汇发〔2020〕14号 Art. 59 (non-domestic individual) or Art. 56 (domestic individual); FX Regulations 条例 Art. 5 and 12; PBOC Order No. 3 Art. 13
requirements: Passport (valid ID)
Source-of-funds documents for the amount: employment contract, payslips, and the PRC individual income tax payment record (税务凭证 / 完税凭证) — Art. 59 expressly includes tax vouchers
Bank's own authenticity review under 条例 Art. 12 and Art. 68
caps: No USD 50,000 cap is stated for this documented conversion. Art. 54 puts the USD 50,000 annual facilitation quota on individuals' FX SALES and DOMESTIC individuals' FX PURCHASES; Art. 59 handles a non-domestic individual's documented current-account purchase separately. A holder of a PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID may instead use the quota (Art. 59 second sentence).
pros: Lawful and expressly provided for in the current rule text
No published quota cap for documented current-account income
Once the money is in your own FX account, Art. 65(1) lets a non-domestic individual remit it abroad on ID alone
cons: The bank, not you, decides whether the paper is sufficient (Art. 68 lets it refuse)
Requires an unbroken tax and employment paper trail for the whole balance
Bank fee is capped but the FX spread scales with the amount
Chinese banks may require the receiving account name to match exactly
steps: Ask the bank for its written list of required documents for a non-resident/foreign-individual current-account conversion of this amount.
Assemble the tax payment record for the same period as the funds (税务凭证/完税凭证) plus contracts and payslips.
Convert CNY→USD at the bank counter or in online banking; keep the 结汇/购汇 slip (水单).
Either remit directly (step 5) or park the USD in your own 外汇储蓄账户, then remit under Art. 65(1).
Send the wire with your name and address exactly as on the US account; choose SHA/OUR consciously (OUR + 'Pay Exact' costs CNY 200 at HSBC).
Keep the SWIFT confirmation, the Chinese conversion slip and the tax vouchers — they are the evidence for both FBAR/8938 and any later audit.
unverified: The FX spread your particular bank will apply (commercial, not published as a rule)
Whether your specific documents will be accepted

name: Remit a foreign-currency balance you already hold
verdict: Cheapest if the account is already in USD
who: Only if the balance is already foreign currency in your own FX savings account
legal_basis: Current Account FX Business Guidelines 2020 Art. 65(1); PBOC Order No. 3 Art. 14
requirements: Funds already in a foreign-currency account in your own name
Valid ID at the counter (Art. 65(1) requires no amount cap and no transaction documents)
caps: No amount cap stated for a non-domestic individual remitting from an FX account (Art. 65(1)). Cash is different: USD 10,000/day with documents above that (Art. 65(2)).
pros: No conversion spread at this step — the CNY→USD conversion already happened earlier
Only the wire fee applies
The rule text requires ID only, not a document bundle
cons: Only works to the extent the money is already in FX — does not solve a CNY balance
The original CNY→FX conversion would itself have carried a spread
steps: Confirm with the bank whether the balance is CNY or a foreign currency, and in which account type.
If FX: instruct the outward remittance under Art. 65(1) with your passport.
If the bank asks for source documents anyway, supply them; the rule permits a bank to refuse a suspicious transaction (Art. 68).
Reconcile the amount received against the amount sent to measure the true all-in deduction.
unverified: Whether your balance is CNY or FX — a private fact I must not assume

name: HSBC Global Transfer to your own HSBC account abroad
verdict: Lowest published fee, but only HSBC-to-HSBC
who: HSBC China customer who also holds an HSBC account in the US
legal_basis: HSBC China tariff 2.2.6.1; the underlying conversion still needs 汇发〔2020〕14号 compliance
requirements: HSBC China account at Advance/Premier/Private Banking tier
HSBC account in your own name in the US (2.2.6.1 covers self-name transfers)
The same conversion documentation as R01 for the CNY→USD leg
caps: Tariff states no amount cap. The FX-conversion rules still apply before any transfer.
pros: Premier: free; Advance: USD 20 per transaction (tariff 2.2.6.1)
One institution on both ends can shorten the correspondent chain
cons: Requires HSBC on both ends
The free/discounted tier requires a CNY 500,000 relationship balance or equivalent (tariff Important Note 3)
Still needs the Art. 59 documentation for the conversion itself
steps: Confirm your HSBC China tier and whether a US HSBC account exists in your name.
Complete the documented conversion (R01 steps 1–3).
Use Global Transfer to Self; the tariff price applies per transaction, not per dollar.
Confirm receipt and record any deduction.
unverified: HSBC US incoming-wire fee (not verified this session)

name: Withdraw USD cash abroad on a mainland bank card (ATM)
verdict: Small amounts only — hard annual cap
who: Anyone holding a mainland-issued RMB or foreign-currency bank card
legal_basis: SAFE Notice 汇发〔2017〕29号 Arts. 1 and 4
requirements: Mainland-issued bank card
Overseas ATM that accepts the card network
caps: CNY 100,000 equivalent per person per calendar year across all your cards (supplementary cards included); CNY 10,000 equivalent per card per day. Exceeding the annual cap suspends overseas cash withdrawals for the rest of that year AND the following year (Art. 1).
pros: No up-front document bundle
Useful for living costs rather than repatriation
cons: Cannot move USD 400,000 — the annual ceiling is about USD 14,958 at the 2026-11-10 BOC rate
Breaching the cap triggers a suspension, and card-lending to evade is expressly prohibited (Art. 1)
ATM operator fees and card FX pricing are set commercially and were not verifiable
steps: Check the card's daily and annual limits with the issuing bank.
Withdraw at an ATM in the US; keep every receipt.
Track cumulative withdrawals against the CNY 100,000 annual ceiling.
Do not use anyone else's card and do not lend yours (Art. 1).

name: Spend the CNY directly on US expenses with the card
verdict: Avoids conversion, but you never receive USD
who: Anyone who can pay US merchants with a mainland card
legal_basis: Current Account FX Business Guidelines 2020 Art. 76(5) (domestic cards used abroad, repaid by FX purchase)
requirements: Merchant that accepts UnionPay or the card network
caps: Merchant and card limits apply; no regulator cap stated for purchases.
pros: No conversion paperwork
Buys goods and services at the point of need
cons: Does not produce a USD balance you control
Card FX markup and any foreign-transaction fee apply to every purchase
Merchant acceptance of UnionPay in the US is uneven
steps: Test a small purchase to see the posted rate and any fee.
Compare the posted CNY cost against the BOC published rate to measure the markup.
Use only for expenses you would incur anyway.

name: Emigration asset transfer (移民财产转移)
verdict: For pre-emigration assets — needs cancelled hukou
who: A person who emigrated from the mainland (or settled in HK/Macau) and is moving assets owned BEFORE acquiring emigrant status
legal_basis: Provisional Measures on Individuals' Outward Asset Transfers (个人财产对外转移售付汇管理暂行办法) Arts. 2, 6, 8, 10, 11
requirements: Cancelled PRC household registration certificate (户籍注销证明) from the police
Proof of settling abroad issued or authenticated by a Chinese embassy/consulate
Property-rights documents and the tax certificate / 完税凭证 from the tax authority
One application for the entire amount
caps: Staged by rule: first remittance ≤ half; after one year ≤ half of the remainder; after two years the balance. Total ≤ RMB 200,000 may go in one approved remittance. Approval level: ≤ RMB 500,000 local SAFE; above that SAFE headquarters.
pros: Designed exactly for moving a whole lawful estate abroad
Explicit legal pathway with defined documents
cons: Requires having given up PRC household registration — a one-way step
Two-year staging for large amounts
SAFE HQ approval above RMB 500,000
Bank must remit to your own account abroad; no cash payout in China
steps: Confirm you hold the 户籍注销证明 and embassy-authenticated settlement proof.
Obtain the tax certificate for the assets from the competent tax authority.
File one application with the SAFE branch where your household was registered.
After approval, take the 核准件 to the designated bank for the first tranche.
Repeat within the staged limits (≤ half, then ≤ half of the remainder after a year, then the balance).
unverified: Eligibility depends on private facts (whether you ever held PRC hukou)

name: Inheritance asset transfer (继承财产转移)
verdict: Only for a lawful inheritance of a mainland estate
who: A foreign citizen (or HK/Macau resident) who has lawfully inherited a mainland estate
legal_basis: Provisional Measures on Individuals' Outward Asset Transfers Arts. 2, 9, 10, 11
requirements: Proof of inheritance (will/probate/bank records), notarised if not already
Deceased's property-rights documents and the tax certificate from the tax authority where the estate is
Proof of settling abroad authenticated by a Chinese embassy/consulate
One application for all property inherited from the same person
caps: Same approval thresholds as R06 (≤ RMB 500,000 local SAFE; above, SAFE HQ). Separate applications for different deceased persons.
pros: Clear statutory route for inherited funds
Can be remitted in one or several tranches
cons: Only applies to inherited property, not your own savings
Notarisation and tax certificates take time
Different deceased persons cannot be combined
steps: Collect the inheritance documents and the deceased's property documents.
Obtain the tax certificate / 完税凭证.
Apply to the SAFE branch where the deceased was registered.
Remit through the designated bank to your own account abroad.

name: Sell mainland property, then repatriate the proceeds
verdict: Capital-account route with its own approvals
who: Owner of mainland real estate selling as a foreign individual
legal_basis: PBOC Order No. 3 Art. 22 (non-domestic individual buying commercial housing, own-use principle) and the property FX rules it cross-refers to
requirements: Completed sale with title transfer and tax paid
Bank/SAFE review of the capital-account documentation
Proof the property was acquired lawfully
caps: Not determined by the documents I verified this session — the specific property-repatriation rules were not re-read here.
pros: Converts an illiquid asset into a remittable balance
Tax on the gain is assessed on the sale, separately
cons: Property-specific approvals on top of everything else
Market and transaction risk; selling is slow
The precise repatriation document list is unverified in this session
steps: Obtain the property-specific document list from the bank and the local SAFE branch before listing.
Complete the sale and settle all taxes.
Apply for the outward transfer of the net proceeds.
Remit to your own account abroad.

name: Entrust a near relative to act for you within their own quota
verdict: Lawful for genuine family support; not a quota pool
who: Where genuine family support or a documented transaction exists
legal_basis: Current Account FX Business Guidelines 2020 Arts. 61 and 62
requirements: Entrustment with both IDs, a power of attorney and a near-relative relationship document (household register, marriage certificate, birth certificate)
A genuine underlying transaction or support obligation
caps: Within-quota agency is limited to the relative's own USD 50,000 facilitation quota, and only for genuine purposes. Using relatives' quotas to move YOUR money is the prohibited 分拆 (Art. 62).
pros: Practical for genuine support payments to family
Expressly permitted with the right paperwork
cons: Cannot be used to multiply your own quota — that is the exact conduct Art. 62 targets
Both sides risk the '关注名单' watchlist and a 3-year enhanced review
steps: Confirm the transfer is genuine support, not a split of your own balance.
Prepare the power of attorney and relationship proof.
The relative applies within their own quota for the genuine purpose.
Keep the support rationale documented.

name: Split the balance across relatives' USD 50,000 quotas
legal_basis: Current Account FX Business Guidelines 2020 Art. 62 (anti-splitting); FX Regulations 条例 Art. 39; PBOC Order No. 3 Art. 7
cons: Art. 62: individuals may not evade quota or authenticity management by splitting; the offender goes on the '关注名单' (watchlist) for the year plus two more
Lenders of their quota get a risk warning, then the watchlist on a repeat
逃汇 exposure under 条例 Art. 39: fine up to 30% of the amount, or 30% up to the equivalent amount if serious
Taints the relatives' records too
steps: Do not do this.

name: Underground bank, hawala or a private FX dealer
legal_basis: FX Regulations 条例 Arts. 45 and 39 (criminal liability referred to in both)
cons: 条例 Art. 45: private or disguised FX trading — warning, confiscation of illegal gains, fine up to 30% (30%–100% if serious), plus criminal liability
条例 Art. 39: moving funds abroad in evasion — fine up to 30%, or 30% to the equivalent amount if serious
No legal recourse if the counterparty disappears
steps: Do not do this.

name: Carry USD cash out in person
verdict: Legal only in small amounts; impractical
who: Traveller carrying their own converted cash
legal_basis: Provisional Measures on Carrying FX Cash Across the Border 汇发〔2003〕102号 Arts. 3, 5, 7; 条例 Art. 42; CBP currency reporting
requirements: Conversion and cash withdrawal inside China (bank 携带证 above USD 5,000)
US FinCEN Form 105 above USD 10,000
caps: China: ≤ USD 5,000 no permit; USD 5,000–10,000 bank 携带证; above USD 10,000 a SAFE-branch permit, and in principle not above USD 10,000 at all (Art. 7). US: report amounts over USD 10,000 on FinCEN 105. China penalty for illegal carriage: warning plus fine up to 20% (条例 Art. 42).
pros: No wire fee
Immediate
cons: Hard limit of about USD 10,000 per trip
Physical loss/theft risk
US declaration obligation and seizure risk if not filed
Carrying USD 400,000 is not lawful in one trip and is unsafe in any case
steps: Convert at the bank and request cash with a 携带证 if between USD 5,000 and 10,000.
Declare to CBP on FinCEN 105 if bringing in more than USD 10,000.
Never split cash among travellers to stay under thresholds — CBP aggregates family/group amounts (S13).
unverified: Whether any bank will issue a 携带证 for your amount

name: Third-party remittance platform (Wise-type)
verdict: No verified path from a mainland CNY balance
pros: Would be cheap if it existed for this corridor
cons: I found no official source confirming that a mainland-bank CNY balance can be sent to the US through such a platform
Any such flow still has to satisfy the same Chinese conversion rules
Prior sessions cited a platform help page; that is a company page, not a regulator, and it was not re-verified here
steps: Verify the corridor directly with the provider and your bank before relying on it.
unverified: Whether the corridor exists at all for a mainland personal CNY balance

name: Move it through an investment channel (QDII / QDLP / Stock Connect)
verdict: Does not put USD in your hands
legal_basis: PBOC Order No. 3 Art. 17 (domestic individual may invest abroad through qualified domestic institutional investors)
requirements: Eligibility set by the institution and the scheme
pros: A lawful way to hold overseas exposure
cons: The money stays inside the domestic scheme — selling does not remit USD to you
Stock Connect is a closed loop by design
Not a repatriation method
unverified: Whether any scheme permits personal remittance of proceeds

name: Buy crypto / USDT inside China and sell abroad
verdict: Not assessed — status not re-verified this session
cons: PRC crypto trading is widely described as prohibited, but I did not re-read the PBOC notice in this session, so the status is flagged rather than asserted
Even if a channel existed, moving value this way to avoid FX rules would engage 条例 Arts. 39 and 45
unverified: Legal status of crypto conversion in the PRC
